name: Rune-Inscribed Tablet
summary: The Rune-Inscribed Tablet is a summoning missive delivered to aspiring shamans training in the Valley of Trials. Sent by Shikrik, it invites promising initiates to begin formal instruction in communing with the spirits and commanding the elemental forces of earth, fire, water, and air.

sections.title: A Call to the Spirits
sections.body: After proving their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials, fledgling shamans are handed a carved stone tablet by Gornek. The runes upon it serve as an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer, signaling that the initiate is ready to look beyond simple physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world.

sections.title: Spiritual Leadership in the New Horde
sections.body: Shamanism occupies a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. As Shikrik teaches, shamans draw their power from the four elemental forces and their strength from ancestral spirits. Emulating Warchief Thrall, shamans are expected to be spiritual guides and bulwarks of wisdom for their communities, offering protection to the settlements taking root across Durotar.

faq.answer: It is an inscribed stone tablet passed to novice shamans by Gornek in the Valley of Trials. It carries a summons from the shaman trainer Shikrik, urging the young adventurer to formalize their training in spiritual and elemental arts.

Shikrik is the shaman trainer stationed near the mouth of the Den in the Valley of Trials. She guides new orc and troll shamans in mastering the elements and understanding their duty as spiritual leaders within the Horde.

faq.q: Why does Shikrik invoke Thrall when speaking to new shamans?
faq.answer: Warchief Thrall led the revival of ancestral shamanism after the demonic corruption of the Old Horde. Shikrik points to Thrall as the quintessential example of a shaman's duty: balancing elemental harmony with guiding and protecting his people.
Shikrik stands just outside the entrance to the Den on the eastern side of the Valley of Trials, ready to teach novice shamans their early techniques.
Gornek, who oversees the initial trials of newcomers arriving in the Valley of Trials, delivers the tablet once an initiate has proven their basic mettle.

faq.q: What core philosophy does Shikrik teach?
faq.answer: Shikrik stresses that a shaman's raw power is drawn from fire, earth, water, and air, while their endurance and resolve stem from the ancestral spirits. Shamans are expected to offer wisdom and defense to whatever towns or warbands they join.

angles.text: This tablet marks your formal initiation into the shamanic path, charging you to balance the elemental powers and serve as a beacon of ancestral guidance.
The tablet reflects the modern orcish return to ancestral shamanism championed by Thrall, leaving behind the dark warlock legacies of the demonic past.
Darkspear trolls practicing shamanism find common ground with orc mentors like Shikrik, blending their ancestral communion with the Horde's shared elemental traditions.
Shamanism is the moral and spiritual backbone of the new Horde, offering a compass of honor and balance across the harsh frontier.
